## Geometric sources on the spherical-polar grid {#sec-ch04-sphsrc}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- The part of the curvature that is not a difference of face fluxes, added after the divergence.
- Switch: none; it is what the spherical-polar coordinate does instead of the Cartesian pass-through.
- The radial source carries the centrifugal terms of the two tangential velocities.
- The radial pressure force uses the face pressures when a solver provides them.
- Areas and volume are exact integrals, not midpoint values.
:::

In curvilinear coordinates the divergence of a tensor is not a difference of face fluxes alone: the basis
vectors turn from face to face, and the leftover is a source. The coordinate object adds it on top of the same
divergence every grid uses, which is why @sec-ch04-divergence can be written once for all geometries.

### Derivation

The geometric factors are built once in the coordinate's own buffers and the source is assembled at
`forward` ([`spherical_polar.cpp:224-250`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L224-L250)). The radial source is the centrifugal pair

$$
S_1 = \frac{A_{23}}{V}\,\rho\,(v_\theta^2 + v_\phi^2),
$$ {#eq-ch04-sphsrc-src1}

at `coord_src1_i` ([`spherical_polar.cpp:243-244`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L243-L244)): a parcel moving tangentially at constant radius needs an inward
force to stay there, and in a radial momentum equation written in fluxes that force appears as a source. The
coefficient is a ratio of the cell's own tangential area to its volume, not a nominal $1/r$, so the identity
survives on a stretched radial grid.

The areas and volume themselves are exact integrals of the metric, not midpoint approximations:
`face_area1` ([`spherical_polar.cpp:178-183`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L178-L183)) for the radial face, `cell_volume` ([`spherical_polar.cpp:200-211`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L200-L211)) for
the volume, which carries the exact $(r_+^3 - r_-^3)/3$. `[C3]` shows what that buys: the midpoint form
$r^2h$ would be short by $h^3/12$ per unit solid angle, so the exact form removes a second-order volume error
that would otherwise appear in every tendency. `[C2]` then confirms that the areas and volume together
reproduce $\nabla\!\cdot\!(r\hat r) = 3$ to $3.6\times10^{-15}$ over a test block, which is the identity the
cubed-sphere volume test asserts cell by cell.

The radial pressure force is the part with a choice in it. With a solver that returns a face pressure the force
can be built from those face values; without one it is a plain difference. The code comment at
`exact_x1` ([`spherical_polar.cpp:246-251`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L246-L251)) states the consequence carefully: with the face pressures the
pressure force is the $r^2$-weighted average of the gradient, which balances $g\rho$ for a hydrostatic column
of $r^2$ means, while the plain difference balances $g\langle\rho\rangle$ instead. Which of those is wanted is
the subject of chapter 5, and the exact-centroid switch that selects it belongs there, not here.

### Numerical method

The source is added after `CoordinateImpl::forward` has produced the divergence, at
[`spherical_polar.cpp:233`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L233), so the flux part and the source part are never mixed. The shallow-water
equation of state takes a different branch at `eos_type` ([`spherical_polar.cpp:245`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L245)), since it has no pressure
row of the kind the force needs.

### Limits

1. **The pressure force depends on the solver.** A solver that returns no face pressure gets the plain
   difference, so the balance the column achieves depends on a key in a different section of the deck. The
   consequences are chapter 5's subject.
2. **Only the radial source is covered here.** The tangential sources and their metric coefficients are part of
   the same `forward` and are described with the grid they belong to in chapter 3.
